transcript: If you didn't know Aubrey Plaza plays the saxophone, I can confirm it is the case. In Let's Love! by Ethan Coen, she and the rest of a uniformly excellent ensemble explore love in all its silly and raunchy glory. It's a trio of one-acts, each more outlandish than the last, but the mood is generally lighthearted and quirky. The charm of this piece is that it doesn't take itself too seriously. The characters are all decently ordinary, we're just seeing them in some of their most dramatic situations. The third and final story really takes it to another level, but I will obviously not spoil it here. I was pleasantly surprised by this, as I feel like it's hard to find comedy of a high quality that still maintains a sense of humility. I guess what I mean is that this knows what it is and it doesn't need to justify itself by shoehorning in overly highbrow jokes. It's just fun and it's a little out there, which may make it somewhat polarizing, but it worked for me. I was especially impressed by the casting — everyone here does a lot with a relatively small amount of stage time, especially the musician-emcee who graces us with some interludes between each act. I will say, I think tickets are a little steep for what this is, but it's a small venue and a nonprofit, so I give them some grace. With that, another playbill for my collection.
